doc.title: Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Oneonta, New York, December 28, 2005

title: Upcoming concerts and CDs with the Harmony Ensemble
summary: New CDs, the Madison Avenue church concert, Steve Richmond, and Grofe's Gallodoro Serenade.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Okay. What’s coming up in the near future?
Oh JoAnn you tell him. We just broke the ice.

Okay here. Here I am with the short term memory, and I’m about to say, duh. Well actually there’s a lot of things going on. We’re about to release the “Saxophone Contrasts” album as a CD, which people have been looking for for a long time. We just released a different CD “The Infinite Gallodoro.” What’s real cool about it is for people that are interested in what we were talking about, like carrying forth into old age what you love to do. It has one CD of his playing today, which is recorded last summer, and the other CD is his older playing. So it’s a kind of comprehensive type of thing. So we have those two things CD-wise in the works, plus all the other stuff that needs to get out there and get promoted. In terms of concerts coming up, Al will be in New York City at the Madison Avenue Presbyterian Church on April 2 at 3 P.M. And the orchestra is the Harmony Ensemble of New York.

Under the conductor Steve Richmond. And what Steve does is take old arrangements, what he’s taking Paul Whiteman arrangements, and he’s replicating them very authentically so that’s why he had contacted Al. Originally he contacted him two years © Fillius Jazz Archive -19-

ago and Al did a recording with him of “Fascinating Rhythm” which was from an old Whiteman arrangement. And they also recorded the “Gallodoro Serenade” with Lincoln Mayorga on piano. It was written for Al by Ferde Grofe back in the 1950s.
So this is really the New York City premier performance.

Yeah. Steve Richmond had told me that he’s working on it now to get that on to CD. So there’s a lot of different stuff. We perform a lot locally. We had Christmas parties, nursing homes, we’ll be at Justin’s in Albany and Cafe Lena in Saratoga. Al, hopefully, will be traveling somewhere. We’re always working on stuff.
All right. Broke that ice. It’s a famous place. Nick Brignola used to play there.
Nick Brignola played there, yeah, a lot of people. So they deserve you.
